title: Enforcement Rule of the Erosion Control Works Act
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Rule is to prescribe matters delegated by the Erosion Control Works Act and its Enforcement Decree and matters necessary for their enforcement. <Amended 2005.5.11, 2008.2.1>

Article 1-2 (Details of Surveys of the Actual Conditions of Degraded Land)
(1) A survey under Article 3-3 of the Erosion Control Works Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”) shall include the following:
1. Basic survey:
(a) Location and scale of degraded land;
(b) Characteristics of degraded land and causes of degradation;
(c) Surrounding conditions, including housing and farmland near degraded land;
(d) Whether erosion control works are necessary;
(e) Other matters deemed necessary by the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service.
2. Detailed survey:
(a) The degree of risk of soil and stone outflow, collapse, or erosion of degraded land;
(b) Characteristics of individual factors causing degraded land, including ground and forest conditions on and near degraded land;
(c) Other matters deemed necessary by the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service.
(2) A basic survey under paragraph (1) 1 shall use either of the following methods:
1. Direct on-site investigation;
2. Remote sensing using aircraft, satellites, etc., or indirect investigation through opinion surveys, data, literature, etc.
(3) A detailed survey under paragraph (1) 2 shall, in principle, use the method under paragraph (2) 1, but may also use the method under subparagraph 2 of that paragraph.
[This Article newly inserted 2009.3.26]

Article 2 (Designation of Erosion Control Areas) Where the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, a Metropolitan City Mayor, the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, a Do Governor, or the Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as “Mayor/Do Governor”), or the head of a regional forest service designates or changes an erosion control area under Article 4 of the Act, he or she shall prepare and retain the following documents: <Amended 1995.12.29, 1999.4.1, 2002.4.19, 2005.5.11, 2006.1.26, 2008.2.1, 2009.3.26, 2017.11.15>
1. Register of erosion control area designations (attached Form No. 1);
2. Drawing of the designated erosion control area (attached Form No. 2).

Article 2-2 (Establishment of a Database for Maintenance and Management of Erosion Control Dams)
(1) A database established and operated under Article 6-2 (1) of the Act for the systematic maintenance, management, and safety inspection of erosion control dams (hereinafter referred to in this Article as “database”) shall be established and operated in connection with the forest disaster information system under Article 11 of the Forest Disaster Prevention Act (hereinafter referred to in this Article as “forest disaster information system”). <Amended 2026.1.30>
(2) The database shall include the following matters:
1. General information on erosion control dams, including construction location and year;
2. Construction information, including the type and scale of erosion control dams (including their design drawings, photographs, etc.);
3. Results of feasibility assessments under Article 7-3 of the Act for installation, etc. of erosion control dams;
4. Results of safety inspections and safety measures for erosion control dams;
5. Other matters necessary for the maintenance and management of erosion control dams.
(3) Mayors/Do Governors or heads of regional forest services shall enter the matters listed in paragraph (2) through the forest disaster information system by the end of February of the following year, as of December 31 each year. <Amended 2026.1.30>
(4) The specialized institutions to which the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service may entrust establishment and operation of the database under Article 6-2 (3) of the Act shall be the institutions or organizations under the subparagraphs of Article 19.
(5) Matters necessary for establishing and operating the database other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4) shall be determined and publicly notified by the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service.
[This Article newly inserted 2015.7.15]

Article 3 (Design and Construction Standards for Erosion Control Works) The design and construction standards for erosion control works under Article 7-2 (2) of the Act shall be as set out in the attached Table. <Amended 2014.2.14>
[This Article newly inserted 2002.4.19]
[Title amended 2014.2.14]

Article 4 (Duties of Forest Engineering Technicians)
(1) The scale of erosion control works for which a forest engineering technician under attached Table 3 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Promotion and Management of Forest Technology (hereinafter referred to as “forest engineering technician”) must be assigned under Article 8 (1) of the Act shall be a construction cost of at least 50 million won per project. <Amended 1995.8.30, 2007.3.28, 2008.2.1, 2018.11.29>
1. Deleted. <2008.2.1>
2. Deleted. <2008.2.1>
(2) The duties of forest engineering technicians shall be as follows: <Amended 1995.8.30, 2005.5.11, 2007.3.28, 2008.2.1, 2018.11.29>
1. Special-grade, advanced-grade, and intermediate-grade forest engineering technicians: Design, construction, construction guidance, and supervision of erosion control works;
2. Entry-grade forest engineering technicians: Design, construction, and construction guidance for erosion control works with a construction cost of less than 200 million won per project.
(3) A person who assigns a forest engineering technician to an erosion control works site under paragraph (1) shall ensure that the technician does not leave the site without just cause and shall replace the technician if he or she is deemed unable to perform the duties due to a mental or physical disability or other reason. <Amended 1995.8.30, 2007.3.28, 2008.2.1>
[Title amended 1995.8.30, 2007.3.28]

Article 5 (Notice of Investigations) Notice under Article 5 (1) and (2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Erosion Control Works Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Decree”) shall be in attached Form No. 5. <Amended 2002.4.19, 2008.2.1, 2014.2.14>
[Title amended 2014.2.14]

Article 6 (Application for Compensation for Loss)
(1) An application for compensation for loss under Article 7 (1) of the Decree shall be in attached Form No. 6. <Amended 2008.2.1>
(2) A determination of the compensation amount under Article 7 (2) of the Decree shall be in attached Form No. 7. <Amended 2008.2.1>
(3) Upon determining the amount of compensation for loss, the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a national forest management office of a regional forest service shall enter its details in a register of compensation determinations in attached Form No. 8. <Amended 1995.12.29, 2006.1.26, 2008.2.1, 2009.3.26>
(4) The register of compensation determinations under paragraph (3) shall be prepared and managed in a manner enabling electronic processing, unless there is a special reason that makes electronic processing impossible. <Newly inserted 2008.2.1>

Article 7 (Application for Adjudication) An application for adjudication under Article 8 of the Decree shall be in attached Form No. 9.

Article 8 (Travel Expenses for Appraisers and Witnesses) Travel expenses for appraisers and witnesses under Article 10 (2) of the Decree shall be the amount payable as travel expenses to Grade V national public officials.

Article 9 (Documents for Permission Applications)
(1) An application for permission under Article 11 of the Decree shall be in attached Form No. 10. <Amended 2008.2.1, 2023.11.17>
(2) “Documents prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs” in the former part of Article 11 of the Decree means the following documents: <Amended 1996.12.28, 2002.4.19, 2005.5.11, 2006.6.30, 2008.2.1, 2008.3.3, 2013.1.23, 2013.3.23, 2023.11.17>
1. One copy of a drawing based on an actual survey of the area for which permission is sought, at a scale from 1:6,000 to 1:1,200 (limited to a survey by a person falling under any item of Article 4 (2) 1 of the Decree);
2. One copy of a statement of timber volume or quantity;
3. One copy of a document proving ownership of the land or the right to use and profit from it (only where this cannot be verified through a certificate of registered matters for the land; a document proving the right to use and profit shall state the scope and duration of that right in detail).
(3) Upon receiving an application under paragraph (1), the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, the Special Self-Governing Province Governor, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu (a head of a Gu means the head of an autonomous Gu; the same applies hereinafter), or the head of a national forest management office of a regional forest service shall verify the certificate of registered matters for the land (only where the applicant is the landowner) through shared use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. <Amended 2008.2.1, 2009.3.26, 2012.1.13, 2013.1.23, 2017.11.15>
(4) Upon granting permission under Article 14 (2) of the Act, the Special Self-Governing City Mayor, the Special Self-Governing Province Governor, the head of the Si/Gun/Gu, or the head of a national forest management office of a regional forest service shall issue a permit in attached Form No. 11. <Amended 2008.2.1, 2009.3.26, 2012.1.13, 2017.11.15>

Article 9-2 Deleted. <2008.2.1>

Article 10 (Method of Distributing Benefits)
(1) Benefits subject to distribution under Article 13 (1) of the Decree shall be benefits in kind arising from erosion control facilities.
(2) Benefits in kind under paragraph (1) shall be distributed within one month after the date they become available for distribution.
(3) Notice of distribution of benefits under Article 13 (2) of the Decree shall be in attached Form No. 12.

Article 11 Deleted. <2012.1.13>

Article 12 (Cancellation of Designation of Erosion Control Areas)
(1) An application for cancellation of the designation of an erosion control area under Article 17 (1) of the Decree shall be in attached Form No. 17. <Amended 2008.2.1>
(2) “Documents prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs” in Article 17 (1) of the Decree means the following documents: <Amended 1996.12.28, 2002.4.19, 2005.5.11, 2006.6.30, 2008.2.1, 2008.3.3, 2013.1.23, 2013.3.23>
1. One copy of the project plan;
2. One copy of a drawing based on an actual survey of the area for which cancellation of erosion control area designation is sought, at a scale from 1:6,000 to 1:1,200 (limited to a survey by a person falling under any item of Article 4 (2) 1 of the Decree);
3. One copy of a document proving ownership of the land or the right to use and profit from it (only where this cannot be verified through a certificate of registered matters for the land; a document proving the right to use and profit shall state the scope and duration of that right in detail).
(3) Upon receiving an application under paragraph (1), the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of the regional forest service shall verify the certificate of registered matters for the land (only where the applicant is the landowner) through shared use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. <Amended 2008.2.1, 2009.3.26, 2012.1.13, 2013.1.23>
(4) Upon cancelling the designation of an erosion control area under Article 20 (1) of the Act and Article 17 (2) of the Decree, the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of the regional forest service shall prepare and keep the following documents: Provided, That the statement assessing reimbursement for cancellation of erosion control area designation under subparagraph 3 is required only for cancellation under Article 20 (1) 2 through 4 of the Act. <Amended 2008.2.1, 2009.3.26>
1. Statement of cancellation of erosion control area designation (attached Form No. 14);
2. Drawing of the area released from erosion control area designation (attached Form No. 15);
3. Statement assessing reimbursement for cancellation of erosion control area designation (attached Form No. 16).

Article 13 (Transfer of Erosion Control Facilities) Notice under Article 18 of the Decree shall be in attached Form No. 18. <Amended 2008.2.1>

Article 14 (Notice of Reimbursement of Expenses) A Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service shall issue to a person intending to obtain cancellation of the designation of an erosion control area under Article 20 of the Act a notice of payment of reimbursement of erosion control works investment expenses in attached Form No. 19, requiring reimbursement of expenses under Article 21 of the Act and Article 19 of the Decree. <Amended 1995.12.29, 2005.5.11, 2006.1.26>

Article 15 (Keeping of Official Registers) The official register to be kept by a Mayor/Do Governor or the head of a regional forest service under Article 20 of the Decree shall be an erosion control works register in attached Form No. 20. <Amended 1995.12.29, 2006.1.26>

Article 16 Deleted. <2026.1.30>

Article 17 Deleted. <2023.4.11>

Article 18 Deleted. <2026.1.30>

Article 19 (Institutions Eligible for Delegation or Entrustment of Research and Development of Erosion Control Works Technology) “Institutions or organizations prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs” in Article 24-3 (2) of the Act means any of the following institutions or organizations: <Amended 2026.1.30>
1. The Korea Forest Disaster Safety Technology Corporation under Article 58 of the Forest Disaster Prevention Act;
2. A cooperative or the federation under the Forestry Cooperatives Act;
3. The Korea Forestry Promotion Institute under the Forestry and Mountain Villages Development Promotion Act;
4. A public-interest corporation related to erosion control works under the Act on the Establishment and Operation of Public Interest Corporations.
[This Article newly inserted 2014.2.14]

Article 20 (Review of Regulations) The Administrator of the Korea Forest Service shall review the appropriateness of the scope of documents to be attached to applications for cancellation of erosion control area designation under Article 12 (2) every three years from January 1, 2017 (meaning before the same date as the base date in every third year) and take measures for improvement, etc.
[Wholly amended 2023.4.11]

■ Enforcement Rule of the Erosion Control Works Act [Attached Table] <Amended 2025. 2. 21.>
Design and Construction Standards for Erosion Control Works (Related to Article 3)

1. Design standards
(a) On-site investigation
1) Before implementing erosion control works, investigate the following common matters:
(a) The area of the erosion control works site, existing obstacles, and their ownership: Investigate by parcel number and land category, and prepare the land acquisition map using the latest cadastral and forest cadastral maps for the area.
(b) The landform and soil conditions of the erosion control works site: Investigate separately for soil and rock; estimate underground bedrock by reference to the topography or surface conditions and nearby cut sections, and, in areas at risk of recurring damage, also conduct ground investigations as necessary.
(c) The location, type, and quantity of structures to be installed and specifications of materials to be used.
(d) The causes and characteristics of degradation of the erosion control works site, including ground conditions, forest conditions, and weather factors (maximum hourly rainfall, continuous rainfall, frequency of heavy rainfall, etc.).
(e) Whether wetlands, rare plants, endemic plants, endangered plants, etc. exist on the erosion control works site or adjoining land.
(f) The feasibility of using heavy equipment, etc. during construction and the extent of cutting (earth excavation) and filling (earth embankment) volumes.
(g) The feasibility of locally obtaining materials required for construction, such as aggregate, stone, and turf, and their durability and environmental properties.
(h) All obstacles to implementing erosion control works, including statutory restrictions on construction.
2) For torrent erosion control works, additionally investigate:
(a) The width and topography of the mountain stream, condition of the stream bed (degree of erosion, gradient, size of constituent material, etc.), and condition of the foundation ground (presence of bedrock, soil properties, degree of weathering, etc.).
(b) The catchment area, hydrological characteristics, groundwater level, floodwater level, etc.
(c) The types and habitats of major aquatic animals and plants living in the stream.

(b) Calculation of the area of erosion control works
1) Calculate the mapped area of erosion control works using horizontal distances and plan areas.
2) Calculate the actual area of erosion control works using slope distances and slope areas.

(c) Preparation of drawings
1) Drafting
(a) Drafting shall follow KSF1001, General Rules for Civil Engineering Drawings.
(b) Use metric units.
(c) Korean characters shall be used in principle, but Chinese characters or foreign languages may be added as necessary.
2) Plan drawings
(a) Use a scale of 1/1,200.
(b) Indicate survey station numbers, locations of major structures, curve radii, etc. on plan drawings; mark the boundaries of privately owned land; and indicate the erosion control work symbols or work names at structure locations.
3) Longitudinal section drawings
(a) Use a vertical scale of 1/100 and a horizontal distance scale of 1/500.
(b) Indicate survey stations, distances between stations, cumulative distances, ground and design elevations, cut and fill heights, cut and fill cross-sectional areas, earthwork volumes, design gradients, etc.
(c) Determine design construction elevations to enable prevention of damage and preservation of the landscape.
4) Cross-section drawings
(a) Use a scale of 1/100.
(b) Indicate cut and fill heights, cut and fill cross-sectional areas, and structures.
(c) Enter cross-sections in order from the lower left toward the top.
(d) Distinguish soil from rock in cut sections, indicating rock portions with estimated lines.
(e) Separately enter quantities for ground and design elevations, cut and fill heights, cross-sectional areas, removal of obstructing trees, slope protection works, etc. for the cross-section at each survey station.
5) Structure drawings
(a) Use a scale of 1/100 in principle; for small structures, another scale may be used. Enter structure details and statements of specifications and quantity calculations for each material.
(b) The design flood discharge shall be at least 1.2 times the maximum flood runoff calculated by either of the following methods; spillways, etc. of transverse structures such as erosion control dams shall be designed for at least 2.0 and not more than 5.0 times that runoff, but a greater multiple may be used in rapid-flow areas:
(1) Calculation by the rational formula using the latest 100-year return-period probable rainfall and flood concentration time;
(2) Calculation by the rational formula using rainfall intensity from extreme heavy rainfall during the last five years (meaning heavy rainfall forecast, warned of, or notified by the Administrator of the Korea Meteorological Administration under Article 47-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety).

(d) Preparation of design documents
1) Prepare design documents in the following order: table of contents, location map, construction description, general specifications, special specifications, proposed construction schedule, statement of relevant cadastral parcels, construction cost calculation, detailed design cost statement, unit work cost table, unit price calculations, various heavy equipment expense calculations, quantity calculations by work type, consolidated lists of required materials, earthwork table, calculation bases, design drawings, etc.
2) For standards applicable to the various unit price calculations necessary for design, apply the standard estimating norms for erosion control determined by the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service; standard construction estimating norms and estimated prices based on completed construction works may also be applied.

2. Construction standards
(a) Carry out construction giving priority to preventing damage to housing, industrial facilities, etc. above and below the erosion control works site.
(b) For mountainous land where a landslide has occurred, apply construction methods, etc. to prevent secondary collapse, erosion, or outflow of soil and stones, including in neighboring areas.
(c) For torrent erosion control works, apply construction methods, etc. to reduce mountain stream flow velocity and mitigate erosion or debris flows.
(d) Install ecological passages in streams with perennial flow and inhabited by fish, etc. to enable fish and other organisms to move.

3. Other matters
Matters necessary for design and construction standards for erosion control works other than those prescribed in subparagraphs 1 and 2 shall be determined and publicly notified by the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service.
